hook: You won't believe how a super El Niño turned the Atacama Desert into 6,560 square miles of flowers.

sections.voiceover: You won't believe how a super El Niño turned the Atacama Desert into 6,560 square miles of flowers.

Record rainfall fueled by a super El Niño hit Chile's Atacama Desert, the world's driest non-polar desert. Could this rare moisture turn the Atacama Desert into a massive, colorful carpet of wildflowers?
The shock is that over 200 plant species grew from seeds and bulbs dormant for decades.
Over 200 plant species suddenly erupted across the Atacama Desert, ending years of extreme, barren dryness.
This rare event covers 6,560 square miles, transforming the Atacama Desert into a vibrant floral landscape.
